prompt.context: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.
prompt.question: FlashPro's growth has stagnated. How would you approach diagnosing the problem and identifying growth opportunities?

clarifying_info.a: Their main product is CamPro, a mounted camera mainly used when playing action sports. It has also recently started being used in other recreational activities.

clarifying_info.q: Where does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro sells its products in the US and internationally, through three channels: Distributors, Retail, and FlashPro's Website.

clarifying_info.q: Does FlashPro manufacture its own products?
clarifying_info.a: No, FlashPro contracts with manufacturers in China.
Gross margin has remained steady at 50%.

clarifying_info.q: What is the US vs. international revenue split?
clarifying_info.a: Over the last 5 years, 60% of camera sales have come from the US. The split is expected to be similar in 2018.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Potential Market in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the number of potential customers (in thousands) in the US action camera market from 2014 actual through 2020 estimated.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Market Penetration in the U.S.
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of the US action camera potential market that has been penetrated, from 2014 actual through 2020 estimated.

exhibits.title: 2016 Action Camera Market Share Distribution
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing market share among action camera competitors. A note states that market share distribution is the same in the US and worldwide and has remained steady for the last 5 years, and that FlashPro is the only company offering wearables.

exhibits.title: New Market Entry Candidates
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four potential new markets (Argentina, Japan, Australia, Sweden) across current market size, expected Year 1 market share, expected annual growth over 3 years, and sales channel distribution (Distributors / Retail / FlashPro Website).

data.note: After Year 3, expected annual growth for all countries is 5%. Dollar amounts in thousands.

framework: Market Analysis: Competitors, Customers (loyalty dynamics), Substitutes, Suppliers (China manufacturers)
Profitability Tree: Revenue = Volume x Price; Costs = COGS + R&D + G&A + Sales & Marketing
Revenue Drivers: US market size and penetration, market share vs. competitors, pricing
Growth Levers: Marketing Mix (4Ps), New Geographies, Product Line Expansion, M&A

questions.prompt: Question 1: What is FlashPro's expected Gross Profit for 2018? (Hand out Exhibits 1, 2, and 3)
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a revenue model using addressable market, penetration rate, and market share from the exhibits, then apply given cost structure. All amounts are in thousands.

math.setup: US addressable market (Exhibit 1 2018E) x penetration rate (Exhibit 2 2018E) x FlashPro market share (Exhibit 3) x camera price = US camera revenue. Scale up for international using the 60/40 US/international split. Apply 50% COGS to get gross profit.
steps: US Camera Sales = 16,000 (addressable market) x 85% (penetration) x 30% (FlashPro share) x $250 (price) = $1,020,000 thousand

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are FlashPro's revenue growth prospects keeping everything constant, and what alternatives could boost the top line? (Refer to Exhibits 1-3)
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that US market growth is slowing (16,000 -> 16,500 -> 16,700 over next 3 years) and penetration is already at 85% heading to 95%, leaving little room for organic US growth. Market share has been steady for 5 years in a highly competitive, brand-loyal market, limiting share gain prospects. From these insights candidate should pivot to identifying growth levers. An excellent candidate organizes levers into: (1) Marketing Mix / 4Ps (product attributes, sales channels, pricing, advertising); (2) New Markets (new geographies, product line expansion); (3) Organic development in-house; (4) Inorganic (M&A / partnerships).

questions.prompt: Question 3: From an economic perspective, which country is most attractive to enter, and what should FlashPro consider before entering? (Hand out Exhibit 4)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Year 3 revenue for each country by growing the Year 1 revenue (current market x Year 1 share) at the annual growth rate for three years. Argentina yields the highest Year 3 revenue and has a favorable channel mix (50% website, which carries higher margins due to no intermediary). An excellent candidate notes the channel mix implication for margins.

math.setup: Year 1 Revenue = Current Market Size x Year 1 Market Share. Grow at annual rate for 3 years: Year 3 Revenue = Year 1 Revenue x (1 + growth rate)^2 (revenue is already at Year 1 in year 1, so two additional years of growth reach Year 3).
steps: Argentina Year 1 = $2,500 x 35% = $875; Year 3 = $875 x (1.10)^2 = $875 x 1.21 = $1,059 (~$1,165 per casebook, using compounding across full 3 year period: $875 x 1.10^2 ≈ $1,059; casebook states $1,165 implying Year 3 = Year 1 x (1+g)^3: $875 x 1.331 = $1,165)
math.answer: Argentina $1,165 > Japan $1,013 > Sweden $951 > Australia $932. Argentina is the most attractive on Year 3 revenue.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should FlashPro consider before entering a new geographic market?

categories.name: Customers
ideas: Local customer habits and preferences for action sports
Brand awareness and loyalty in target market
Willingness to pay at $250 price point

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Local and global competitors already present
Barriers to switching for existing customers

categories.name: Economics & Geopolitics
ideas: Currency risk and exchange rate volatility
Political risk and ease of doing business

categories.name: Operations & Logistics
ideas: Ability to service existing channel partners (distributor vs. retail vs. website)
Supply chain from China manufacturers to new market

recommendation: FlashPro should pursue a geographic expansion strategy to achieve growth, given limited room for incremental US growth

Argentina is the most attractive entry market: it offers the highest Year 3 revenue ($1,165 thousand), a 35% expected Year 1 market share, and a 50% website channel mix that should generate higher margins by eliminating intermediaries
risks: Entry and market development costs have not been factored into the analysis; actual profitability could differ significantly
Year 1 market share assumptions (especially 35% for Argentina) may be aggressive for a new market entrant
Competitive responses in target markets could compress market share or force price reductions
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on the Argentinian market: local competition, customer research, regulatory environment
Assess internal capabilities required for international expansion (local marketing, logistics, after-sales support)
Develop a go-to-market plan including advertising, channel strategy, pricing, and promotions tailored to Argentina
